subject: Runtime telemetry provenance and inter-zone attestation Q&A
messages:
From: David Liao <david.liao@orchidbank.com>

Cc: secops@orchidbank.com

Subject: Runtime telemetry provenance and attestation

Hi Rishi / team,

Thanks for the quick turnaround on the RFP packet. OrchidBank's auditors asked for a focused write-up on runtime telemetry provenance and cross-zone attestation for our planned Dedicated deployment. High-level asks:
- What telemetry (traces, request metadata, kernel-level metrics) do you collect by default vs optional?
- For each telemetry source, can you attest origin, signing, and retention policy?
- How are traces correlated across zones/peers without leaking tenant identifiers?
- Do any telemetry streams contain customer PII or request payload fragments by default?

We need an evidence packet and a short threat summary that explains attack paths (spoofed traces, trace-replay, forged control-plane telemetry) and what mitigations you provide. If you can attach a small sample trace file and the attestation matrix that would speed review.

We'd like to get this answered and a short 30-minute call later today if possible.

Thanks,
David
Director, Infrastructure Security
OrchidBank

(attachment: initial-orchid-asks.pdf)

From: Rishi Malhotra <rishi_malhotra@redwood.ai>
To: David Liao <david.liao@orchidbank.com>
Cc: neha_kapoor@redwood.ai, vanessa_ortiz@redwood.ai, ben_carter@redwood.ai
Date: Tue, 27 Apr 2027 10:05:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Runtime telemetry provenance and attestation

David — thanks for the clear list. High-level responses below; attaching a mapping PDF and a small synthetic trace sample for auditor review. Also attaching an attestation matrix (spreadsheet) that maps claim -> evidence.

Quick summary:
- Telemetry categories:
  * Control-plane audit logs (auth events, operator actions) — signed and retained per customer SLA.
  * Data-plane request telemetry (request metadata, per-token timing metrics) — stored as metadata only (no payloads) unless customer enables full-request logging.
  * Kernel/host metrics (GPU utilization, kernel traces) — aggregated and anonymized; no tenant identifiers.
  * Distributed traces (per-request spans) — include span ids and hashed tenant markers; spans are signed by the local zone's attestation key before export.

- Provenance & signing: we generate an HSM-backed ephemeral signing key per deployment zone (rotated daily). Each trace span contains a zone-signed marker and a short provenance header that auditors can verify against the attestation-matrix.

- PII: by default we do not capture request bodies or user-provided text in telemetry. Customers can opt-in to full-request traces; if enabled, customers control retention and we recommend encryption-at-rest + strict access controls.

- Cross-zone correlation without tenant leakage: we use a deterministic, non-reversible tenant hash (tenant_id -> sha256(salt + tenant_id)) stored in the trace as the marker. Salt is per-customer and stored in the KMS with strict access controls. This allows correlation while preventing reversal.

Next steps: I've looped in Ben for the attack-path details, and Vanessa to confirm SLA/retention language. If this high level looks OK I can package the attestation matrix and a 1-page threat summary for auditors.

Rishi
Head of Product Security
Redwood Inference

Attachments: telemetry-provenance-mapping.pdf, trace-sample-20270427.json, attestation-matrix-ORB.xlsx

From: Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.ai>
To: Rishi Malhotra <rishi_malhotra@redwood.ai>, David Liao <david.liao@orchidbank.com>
Cc: neha_kapoor@redwood.ai, vanessa_ortiz@redwood.ai
Date: Tue, 27 Apr 2027 11:20:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Runtime telemetry provenance and attestation — technical detail

David / team — adding technical detail on the telemetry chain and threat mitigations. Below is an abbreviated provenance model and common attack paths with controls.

Provenance model (sequence):
- 1) Instrumentation emits span with local span_id, start/end timestamps, and tenant_hash.
- 2) Local zone agent stamps span with zone_id and signs span header using zone ephemeral key (HSM).
- 3) Agent forwards to local collector which applies additional enrichment (no raw payloads). Collector appends sequence number and forwards over mTLS to the control-plane ingestion tier.
- 4) Control plane re-signs (aggregated signature) and stores pointers to traces in the telemetry store. Full traces are stored only if customer has enabled full-request logging.

Attack paths & mitigations:
- Forged spans (attacker injects fake spans): prevented by zone-signed span markers; verify signature chain in auditors' tooling.
- Replay of traces to obfuscate events: each span includes a monotonic sequence and collector-level nonce; replays will show inconsistent nonces and can be flagged.
- Trace correlation leaking tenant identifiers: tenant_hash uses a customer-specific salt stored in a KMS. Without the salt the hash cannot be mapped to a tenant. Additionally, we strip any headers that may contain PII before export.
- Compromised agent exporting payloads: agents run in sealed sidecar containers with read-only mounts; agent binaries are hashed at build-time and attested at boot via the enclave attestation flow.

Operational controls we offer:
- Per-customer KMS scoping for salt + key material.
- Audit-only mode: send signed provenance headers to auditors without exposing full traces.
- Retention lock: customer-configurable retention with write-once buckets for mandated timelines.
- Signed evidence bundles: we produce a zip containing signed trace headers + signature chain for a given period for auditor ingestion.

Mini ASCII diagram (zone -> collector -> control plane):
[zone agent] --(signed spans/mTLS)--> [collector (seq/nonce)] --(mTLS)--> [control-plane telemetry store]

Let me know if you want explicit sample verification commands (openssl/verify) and a small python verifier we can hand to your auditors.

Ben Carter
Senior Security Engineer, Redwood Inference

Attachment: attestation-matrix-ORB.xlsx (updated - includes verification steps)
